text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2% today as oil prices climbed on geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and energy supply concerns. A deadly attack on a Saudi airport pushed Brent crude above $106 a barrel, and the Trump administration's consideration of military involvement against Iran-backed Houthis added uncertainty to regional energy flows—factors that generally support higher oil prices and boost the revenues of major oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The stock's broader two-week rally of 8.5% reflects a sharp shift in the oil market backdrop. Discussions around a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, potential easing of energy sanctions, and growing Middle East instability have all pushed global crude prices up significantly (Brent is now $125 per barrel), even as U.S. crude remains more moderate at $96. For a large-scale oil and gas producer, this environment of elevated global oil demand uncertainty and regional supply risks tends to support higher valuations.
